Subject: Renewal procurement: Canary PO split & evidence sprint

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning. To keep the customer experience smooth during your term change and capacity uplift, we propose a two-step procurement path: a small "canary" PO to cover the initial ramp (20% capacity) and a follow-on PO for the remainder once the evidence sprint completes. Benefits:
- Faster initial provisioning (avoid full procurement lag)
- Minimal billing changes for accounting while technical verification runs
- Clear evidence bundle for your procurement team before final commit

I've attached a short plan and checklist (renewal-canary-po-plan.xlsx, evidence-upload-checklist.pdf). Can you confirm whether HelioMed can accept a staged PO flow and whether procurement@heliomed.com should be the recipient for the DocuSign?

Next steps I propose:
1) HelioMed confirms acceptance of staged PO and primary procurement contact
2) Redwood opens a procurement portal ticket and creates the canary PO (net 30)
3) HelioMed uploads evidence artifacts to the shared Drive folder during the sprint (2 weeks)
4) After validation, Redwood issues the final PO and DocuSign for signature

If that sounds good I'll loop in our Finance & Legal leads for the PO template and signatory path.

Thanks,
Sofia

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for laying this out. HelioMed is open to a staged approach, but procurement needs clarity on:
- How the canary PO will appear on our ledger (we prefer a separate PO number for audit)
- Confirmation that the canary PO will not alter pricing tiers for the remainder of the year
- A short list of the evidence artifacts required for validation (logs, proof of isolation, SOC2 excerpt)

procurement@heliomed.com is the right inbox for DocuSign and PO coordination. Can you also confirm who from Redwood will be the signer on the final PO? We typically need the legal name and billing address included up front.

I'll check whether finance wants a 10-day review window after the canary completes.

Best,
Elena Morales
